stories.headline: Satirical Tweet Imagines Trump Backing Medicare for All as Jeffries Says No
stories.hook: A cheeky tweet pictures a wild twist: Trump ready to pass Medicare for All, only for Hakeem Jeffries to block it. The idea hit a nerve amid fresh midterm shifts.
stories.summary: The post by @ostonox, racking up tens of thousands of likes, pokes at Trump's recent talk of 'great healthcare' teamwork with Democrats, who now control Congress from January 2026. Jeffries favors smaller steps like lowering Medicare's age and adding dental coverage, but not full single-payer that scraps most private insurance. Critics like Neera Tanden dismissed it as another Trump feint, citing his ACA repeal efforts, while others saw it as satire spotlighting left-wing strategy debates. Experts note big reforms face vetoes and filibusters, with incremental changes gaining traction.

stories.headline: Senate Republicans Face Base Backlash Over Thune's Stalled Priorities
stories.hook: MAGA supporters vented raw frustration at Senate Majority Leader John Thune, blaming him for blocking key bills and nominees in the final weeks of GOP control.
stories.summary: After Democrats won Senate majorities with a 56-44 edge following midterms, Republicans drew sharp criticism from their base for inaction on priorities like the SAVE America Act, which requires proof of citizenship for voter registration and passed the House multiple times but stalled in the Senate. Posts highlighted over 700 House-passed bills sitting idle and slow progress on 171 Trump nominees, with one user noting just one judge confirmed last week. Critics called Thune the worst GOP leader in history or a traitor, while he defended regular order amid narrow margins; petitions now demand a no-confidence vote as Democrats prepare to take control in January.

stories.headline: Conservatives Blast Sen. Tillis Over Litigation Funding Tax Bill
stories.hook: In his final weeks as a senator, Thom Tillis is drawing fire from fellow conservatives for a bill they say hands Democrats a win by crippling lawsuits against banks.
stories.summary: The Tackling Predatory Litigation Funding Act would slap a 40.8% excise tax on third-party lawsuit financing, which critics like former Justice official Chad Mizelle argue would gut funding for conservative legal battles over debanking by big banks. Figures such as Laura Ingraham and Riley Gaines voiced frustration, with Gaines stressing the need for tools to hold banks accountable, while North Carolina locals called Tillis an embarrassment. Tillis defends the bill as curbing abusive practices and has backed separate anti-debanking measures, but the backlash has Republicans urging leadership to block it before year's end amid his lame-duck retirement.

stories.headline: Americans Split on Affordability Crisis Amid Rising Inflation
stories.hook: Only 17% of adults believe today's children will have it better than their parents, capturing deep economic unease across the board.
stories.summary: President Trump blames high prices on the prior Biden administration, claiming they are now way down, while supporters argue an information operation misled voters on affordability. Critics point to Trump's tariffs and the ongoing Iran conflict, which spiked energy prices with gasoline up 9.1% in September as inflation hit 3.7%. A post-election survey showed voters more likely to blame tariffs than the war itself, reflecting divided views on groceries, energy, and housing costs.

stories.headline: Debate Intensifies Over Trump's Affordability Crisis Claims
stories.hook: Two years into Donald Trump's second term, polls show only 17% of Americans believe kids will have it better than their parents—a stark sign of economic unease.
stories.summary: Social media users fiercely debate whether high costs for gas, groceries, and housing stem from Trump policies like tariffs or lingering Biden-era inflation. Trump counters that his administration inherited the problem and has lowered prices through tax cuts and energy boosts, while critics blame him for ongoing 3.7% inflation above Fed targets. Midterm losses handed Democrats House and Senate control, driven by voter frustration over living costs as the top issue.

stories.headline: GOP Tensions Rise as Congress Nears End with Johnson Urging Attendance
stories.hook: With just 44 days left before Democrats take the Senate majority, Speaker Mike Johnson is calling every Republican back to Washington—except for serious medical issues—to push through key bills.
stories.summary: Johnson's November 20 letter highlights the House passing over 1,000 measures while Senate Democrats blocked nearly 700, stressing the need to advance government funding, the NDAA, and more before January. Conservatives are voicing frustration at Senate Majority Leader John Thune, with President Trump blaming him for stalling military funding and air traffic control reforms, and a White House official citing a held-up $350 billion Pentagon boost. Meanwhile, Rep. Tim Burchett announced his 2028 Senate run in Tennessee, polling strongly and drawing cheers as a conservative fighter. These moves underscore Republican pressure to act aggressively in their final weeks of unified control.

stories.headline: Rep.-Elect Chevalier Challenges Corporate Grip on House Speakership
stories.hook: Fresh off her primary upset, 32-year-old Rep.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier called out corporate capture of the House speakership in a recent interview. Her bold stance drew cheers and criticism alike.
stories.summary: Chevalier, a Democratic Socialist who defeated longtime incumbent Adriano Espaillat to win New York's 13th Congressional District, was one of 11 Democrats who voted against nominating Hakeem Jeffries as speaker in a 251-11 closed-door tally. The Ph.D. student and former public defender's office investigator argued that party leadership must take concrete actions to rebuild voter trust amid fragile faith in institutions. Her comments spotlight tensions in the Democratic Party between progressives seeking campaign finance reform and those favoring unity, as Democrats gear up to control the House with a large majority starting January 3, 2027.

stories.headline: House Democrats Promise Lower Costs and Peace Amid Price Rise Backlash
stories.hook: House Democrats pledged lower costs and an end to foreign wars, but a stark graphic of soaring prices under the prior administration drew swift pushback from skeptics.
stories.summary: Democrats highlighted Republican chaos while promising affordable healthcare and lower costs, alongside claims that they would end what they called Donald Trump's 265-day war with Iran. A Fox Business graphic detailed sharp increases from January 2021 to May 2024, including 20.1% overall inflation, 35.3% home prices, 148% mortgage rates, 46% gas, and 21.5% food prices—figures backed by Bureau of Labor Statistics and USDA data. Critics replied by tying the promises to past Democratic records on inflation, borders, and foreign funding, questioning their credibility in the heated exchange.
